findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above cheese and raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk in cooler. The PIC was informed and these items were rearranged. Ensure staff are following proper storage order guidelines in the future.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed rice stored in the warming table to be stored in a black plastic bag. The PIC was informed that this bag is not food safe, and should not be used for food storage. Furthermore, this plastic is not rated to be heated in a warmer, and may result in melting plastic contaminating the food items within the bag. Ensure food is stored in properly rated containers. Inspector recommends using aluminum foil to protect the warming containers rather than plastic.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant between the counter and wall around the dish machine to be soiled or damaged. The PIC was instructed to wash and sanitize the sealant. If the sealant appears stained or damaged after sanitizing, the silicone will require replacement. Ensure the sealant is in good repair and clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed four sanitizer buckets in the facility measure 0ppm chlorine with a test strip. The PIC was informed. The chemical in sanitizer will evaporate faster than usual in increased temperatures. Ensure staff are monitoring the buckets with test strips and replacing the buckets more frequently. The buckets were replaced during today’s visit.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following cold holding violations in the facility:
1. The prep cooler (tomato 45.2F, probe thermometer)
2. The drawer cooler below the grill (chicken 55.4F, probe thermometer)
3. The upright cooler next to the stairs (shrimp 54.2, probe thermometer)

The facility is experiencing higher than normal temperatures in the kitchen (90.8F ambient) due to an ongoing heat advisory. The walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer were both holding adequate temperatures. All TCS food items from the upright cooler and drawer coolers were moved to the walk-ins. Only the upright cooler was able to reach 41F after leaving the doors sealed. As a temporary solution until temperatures can resolve, time as a control will be used for all TCS foods stored outside of the walk-in cooler and freezer during dinner service. The chef is well informed regarding proper time as a control practices and will also keep food items on an ice bath during service. A follow-up will be conducted tomorrow afternoon during lunch to check cooler temperatures and determine an action plan for combatting the heat in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler, upright cooler near the stairs, and drawer coolers below the grill to be holding food items above 41F during today’s visit. The ambient temperature of the kitchen measured 90.8F. The owner, Bruno, attempted to contact a service technician during today’s visit. In the meantime, these three coolers are not considered adequate for cold holding and alternative cooling must be used. The chef developed a plan to use time as a control for all TCS foods stored outside the walk-in coolers during dinner rush. These trays will be clearly marked with a time of removal from the cooler as well as the four-hour discard time. The inspector will follow-up on cooler repair on July 10, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.
